rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3 report the authors' own UAV survey (Parrot Anafi, 24 May 2019) over a 0.78 ha maize field at Legnaro, NE Italy, and their own prescription-map outputs (Table 2, Figs 5-7). Q2: Section 3 and Table 2 report that, relative to full-field (blanket) spraying, the area to be sprayed from UAV-derived prescription maps ranged from 14.59% to 2.18% of the field for MLC, 18.92% to 3.75% for ANN and 15.82% to 3.49% for OBIA depending on cell size and threshold. Q7: Discussion states that the effectiveness of the prescription maps is closely tied to matching the detection scale (grid cell) with the spraying equipment available, i.e. sprayers capable of section- or nozzle-level control, and that smaller cells gave lower treated areas only where such precision sprayers exist. Q8: Discussion states that no spraying was carried out, that field trials are still needed to validate the maps under operational conditions, that the study did not compare algorithms technically, that cost-effectiveness studies for Italian farms are missing, and that there is a trade-off between herbicide savings and risk of under-treatment.
rows.notes: The study is on maize, not vegetable crops as the passage states. The passage also misreads the numbers: 2.18%-18.92% is the share of the field that would still be sprayed (i.e. an 81-98% reduction in treated area), not the size of the reduction. The study does not say ANN was more efficient; it says ANN had higher detection sensitivity and produced the largest treated areas (least herbicide saving), while MLC was most conservative. Q3: the three classifiers are applied to the same single RGB orthomosaic with no independent ground check of the area reduction, so one method. Q4: the classification accuracies in Table 1 and the classification outputs are taken from the authors' earlier paper (Mattivi et al. 2021), so no intermediate variable measured in this study. Q5/Q6: single field, crop, season and site. Q9: Table 2 gives point values only, no dispersion.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a GIS-based desk analysis of prescription maps from one UAV flight; no herbicide application or yield/weed-control outcome was measured, so support is for the computed reduction in area to be treated only.
